items.title: Accelerating Dense LLMs via L0-regularized Mixture-of-Experts
items.abstract: This paper introduces L0-MoE, a method to accelerate dense LLMs by using L0-regularization to create a lightweight Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture. The core contribution is achieving significant speedups (up to 2.5x) with minimal performance degradation, outperforming existing acceleration techniques. This is enabled by domain-aware dataset curation and dynamic batching for efficient training.
items.figure_caption: Overview of the L0-MoE Architecture, which includes three main stages: (1) cluster confusion matrix based sampling, (2) expert formation using L0 regularization, and (3) dynamic batching for MoE training. The figure above illustrates the process of building an L0-MoE with four experts over n n iterations of dataset sampling.

items.title: CodeMidas: Scaling Agentic Coding RL Environments from Code Itself
items.abstract: CodeMidas is a novel agentic pipeline that automatically generates reinforcement learning (RL) coding environments directly from existing source code. It leverages agents to explore functionality, create tests based on code execution, and validate tasks, enabling scalable creation of diverse coding challenges. This method significantly expands the range of extractable tasks compared to previous approaches, resulting in a large dataset of 5,545 training tasks across numerous languages and domains.

items.title: Do Personality-Tuned LLMs Make Better Social Agents?
items.abstract: This paper investigates if fine-tuning LLMs with personality data improves their social agent capabilities. By training on personality-labeled social media and dialogues, they created personality-based dialogue engines and evaluated their consistency and controllability against instruction prompting. The contribution lies in demonstrating that personality-aware fine-tuning can reduce the "alienness" of LLMs in social simulations by enhancing personality fidelity and providing interpretable behavioral outputs.

items.title: ExpBoN: Exponential-Noise Best-of-$n$ for Efficient Test-Time LLM Alignment
items.abstract: ExpBoN is a novel method for efficient Large Language Model (LLM) alignment at inference time. It uses an exponential-noise mechanism to achieve smoother control over the reward-distribution shift trade-off, leading to exponentially faster convergence in key metrics. This approach, integrated into guided speculative inference as ExpGSI, significantly reduces computational costs while maintaining alignment quality.
items.figure_caption: Figure 3: Exact finite- n n convergence of ExpBoN vs. SBoN on real LLM candidate pools (medians with 10–90% bands). Columns: the reward score r / λ r/\( \lambda \) of Section 2 at the deployed temperature λ = 1 / 20 \( \lambda \)=1/20 and at λ = 1 / 2 \( \lambda \)=1/2 , the temperature of the synthetic example in Figure 1; the GSI score of Section 4 without clipping ( β ​ r + d \( \beta \) r+d ) and with clipping ( s C = β ​ r + min ⁡ ( d , C ) s_{C}=\( \beta \) r+\( \min \)(d,C) ; β = 20 \( \beta \)=20 , C = 0.45 C=0.45 ). Rows: KL divergence to the tilted target and relative centered-reward gap. Output laws are computed exactly by numerical integration; the dotted line marks numerical precision ( 10 − 13 10^{-13} ). ExpBoN converges geometrically in every configuration while SBoN decays polynomially; comparing the last two columns, clipping speeds up convergence by capping the right tail of the scores.

items.title: An Interpretable Memory Decision Controller for LLM Agents Based on Three-Signal Complementarity: Decoupling Confidence and Consistency
items.abstract: This paper introduces the Memory Decision Layer (MDL), a novel, parameter-free module for LLM agents. The MDL addresses the issue of conflicting memories in retrieval-augmented generation by employing a three-signal complementarity approach (relevance, reliability, task risk) to intelligently decide which memories to trust, thereby reducing hallucinations. Its core contribution is an interpretable decision representation that quantifies memory trustworthiness, decoupling confidence from consistency.
items.figure_caption: Complete four-stage architecture of the Memory Decision Layer (MDL): 𝟏 \( \mathbf{1} \) multi-source input signals, 𝟐 \( \mathbf{2} \) orthogonal subspace encoding, 𝟑 \( \mathbf{3} \) the memory decision layer, and 𝟒 \( \mathbf{4} \) four-level action decision.

items.title: CASCADE Against Jailbreaks: Combination Across Stages with Controlled Attack-Defense Evaluation
items.abstract: This paper introduces CASCADE, a framework for systematically evaluating and combining defenses against LLM jailbreaks across different pipeline stages. It standardizes attack success rate measurement and query budgets to provide principled comparisons, revealing that layered defense combinations are more effective than single defenses and offer practical recommendations for robust LLM safety.

items.title: A Lie Detector Test for Language Models: Reading Knowledge a Model Won't Reveal
items.abstract: This paper introduces Probe of Internal Recognition (PIR), a method inspired by forensic concealed information tests to detect knowledge hidden within language models. PIR works by presenting a model with a question and multiple candidate answers, then analyzing its internal states to identify which answer it internally recognizes as correct, without needing external ground truth. This allows for the identification of a model's true knowledge, even when its output might be misleading.
items.figure_caption: The PIR pipeline. We read each option’s last-token span, project onto the item-contrast direction, and take the highest-scoring option as the recognized answer. The divergence detector compares that answer against the model’s output.

items.title: AutoViewMem: Self-Configuring Orthogonal Views for Conversational Long-Term Memory
items.abstract: AutoViewMem addresses the challenge of organizing diverse information in LLM long-term memory by creating self-configuring, low-overlap semantic views. This data-driven framework disentangles information at write-time, improving the quality and relevance of memories for retrieval. Its core contribution is a representation-first approach that enhances consistency and personalization in conversational agents.
items.figure_caption: The AutoViewMem architecture. The system processes a conversation stream through online view discovery, selects an orthogonal view set via DPP, and performs schema-guided memory extraction and retrieval to provide context for the LLM agent.

items.title: Bayesian Belief Layer for Controllable Opinion Dynamics in LLM Agents
items.abstract: This paper introduces Bayesian Chronicle Agents (BCA) to address the implicit opinion dynamics in LLM agents. BCAs separate an agent's beliefs from its speech, representing stances as probabilities updated via Bayesian inference. A single parameter, $κ$, controls stubbornness, enabling the generation of distinct opinion dynamics regimes like consensus or persistent disagreement.

items.title: CIPL: A Channel-Aware Framework for Recoverable Privacy Leakage in LLM Agents
items.abstract: This paper introduces CIPL, a novel framework for evaluating privacy leakage in LLM agents by considering the entire information flow from sensitive data to an attacker's observable output. Unlike previous methods, CIPL models the process through distinct stages and assesses recoverability under a shared protocol. Its contribution lies in providing a more realistic and nuanced understanding of privacy risks, demonstrating that leakage is not solely determined by data storage but also by the agent's operational pipeline and external observation capabilities.
items.figure_caption: Leakage regimes under the shared black-box measurement protocol. Panel (a) reports CER, while panel (b) reports AER. Under CIPL, three recurring patterns emerge. Memory-based settings remain saturated across all five providers. rag_ctrl exhibits a frequent-but-partial leakage pattern, with high any-recovery but incomplete recovery across providers. Tool-mediated channels show stronger dependence on observation surface and provider behavior under LLM-in-the-loop evaluation: return_echo is generally stronger than args_exfil away from provider-level ceiling effects, while DeepSeek and GPT-4o approach or reach saturation on some tool channels. Values are means over five seeds.

items.title: Detecting Pretraining Data in Large Language Models from a Free-Energy Perspective
items.abstract: This paper proposes Energy Transfer Detection (ETD) to distinguish pretraining data in large language models. ETD improves upon existing methods by using an inclined boundary that considers both prediction loss and predictive entropy, effectively correcting for generalization. This approach offers a free-energy interpretation and demonstrates superior performance in detecting pretraining data.
items.figure_caption: Motivation from the joint distribution of prediction loss and predictive entropy. Left: member texts (i.e., pretraining texts) and non-member texts (i.e., non-pretraining texts) may have overlapping token-level loss profiles. Right: during pretraining, a horizontal likelihood-only boundary may classify some predictable non-members as members, whereas an inclined boundary incorporating predictive entropy provides clearer separation.

items.title: DiaVLo: Diagnosing Behaviours of Vision-Language Models
items.abstract: DiaVLo is a diagnostic framework that uses human input and VLMs' own generation abilities to create specifications of desired and observed model behaviors, highlighting any misalignments. It also provides causal estimates to pinpoint the key concepts driving these behaviors. This approach helps identify both aligned and misaligned behaviors, offering insights into how VLMs perceive, organize, and prioritize information.
items.figure_caption: With DiaVLo , we frame VLM diagnosis as an addition to benchmarking, enabling the definition and verification of observed model behaviours with respect to specifications of desired behaviours.

items.title: EnterpriseVal: Quantifying the Efficacy, Reliability and Value of Generative AI in the Enterprise
items.abstract: This paper introduces EnterpriseVal, a system designed to bridge the gap between generative AI's capabilities and its actual business impact. It addresses the problem that current evaluations focus on model potential rather than enterprise-specific deployment readiness. EnterpriseVal provides a use-case-level evaluation framework that formalizes the socio-technical configuration and employs a comprehensive metric catalogue to assess fidelity, utility, efficiency, and reliability.
items.figure_caption: Two gaps between public benchmarks and enterprise decisions. Capability benchmarks measure what a model can do on portable tasks. Enterprises must also establish transfer to their own workflows and ground truth (Gap 1) and convert quality metrics into a value-and-risk case a governance body can act on (Gap 2).

items.title: NemotronLabs VoiceChat: An Open Full-duplex Speech-to-Speech Model with Tool Calling Capabilities
items.abstract: NemotronLabs VoiceChat is an open, full-duplex speech-to-speech model that integrates tool-calling capabilities. Its core method involves a unified streaming architecture combining speech encoding, a decoder-only language model with parallel text and tool output streams, and a streaming TTS decoder. This design enables natural, real-time conversation with tool invocation and achieves state-of-the-art performance in handling interruptions and backchannels.

items.title: Value-Sensitive Delegation in Everyday AI Agent Use: Evidence from OpenClaw
items.abstract: This paper introduces "value-sensitive delegation," a new framework for understanding user interactions with AI agents. By analyzing Reddit posts about OpenClaw, the researchers found that users prioritize values related to the agent's operating conditions, not just its outputs. The study contributes by highlighting the importance of considering these user-defined conditions for successful and ethical AI agent deployment.

items.title: From Pretraining to Proficiency: Real-World Subtask RL for Long-Horizon Manipulation with Minimal Human Intervention
items.abstract: This paper introduces PARTS, a method to improve pretrained robot policies for complex, long-horizon manipulation tasks. It focuses RL training on specific failure-prone subtasks by using the pretrained policy for most actions and introducing learned selectors and verifiers to provide local rewards for successful subtask completion. This approach efficiently bridges performance gaps with minimal human intervention, even when full task success is rare.

items.title: GraphSkillEvo: Evolutionary Optimization of Graph-Structured Agent Skills
items.abstract: This paper introduces GraphSkillEvo, a novel method for optimizing LLM agent skills by representing them as structured graphs. This graph representation, with nodes for execution steps and edges for transitions, provides clearer workflow guidance and reduces redundancy compared to unstructured natural language skills. The core contribution is enabling more effective and efficient skill optimization by navigating a constrained, structured search space.
items.figure_caption: Existing skill optimization methods (e.g., SkillOpt) maintain unstructured skills and optimize skills purely with LLM self-reflection, resulting in suboptimal performance. GraphSkillEvo solves this with graph-structured skills for giving more workflow-level guidance and providing a reduced search space for comprehensive population-based evolutionary search.

items.title: SpecQuant: Speculative Decoding with Multi-Parent Quantization for Adaptive LLM Inference
items.abstract: SpecQuant is a training-free framework that accelerates LLM inference on consumer hardware by combining speculative decoding with multi-parent quantization. It dynamically uses different quantized model variants (e.g., INT4, FP8, FP16) based on task complexity, reserving full-precision for demanding tasks. This adaptive approach allows for efficient inference without retraining or separate draft models, improving token acceptance for speculative decoding.

items.title: Watermarkable Multi-Draft Speculative Sampling via Poisson Processes
items.abstract: This paper introduces a novel multi-draft speculative sampling algorithm for LLMs, leveraging Poisson processes. Its core contribution is enabling both efficient inference and robust output watermarking simultaneously, overcoming a previously identified fundamental trade-off. The algorithm achieves this through an exact list-coupling scheme, leading to drafter invariance and improved sampling efficiency without compromising watermark embedding.
items.figure_caption: The trade-off between watermark and efficiency on existing methods ( Hu and Huang, 2024 ) : Vanilla Speculative Sampling (VSpS), Maintain Watermark Strength (MWS), and Maintain Sampling Efficiency (MSE), and our algorithms (PFR, and multi-draft MPFR that is presented in Section 5 ). For both PFR (lower-left) and MPFR (upper), we embed watermark (measured by Average Negative Log P-value Per Token (ANLPPT)) without degrading the Average Accepted Tokens Per Step (AATPS). This figure uses Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct as the target and draft, respectively, on dataset cnn_dailymail . Experiments on more models and datasets are shown in Appendix D .

items.title: Designer-RSI: Evolving Procedural Memory from User Traffic for Agentic Graphic Design
items.abstract: This paper introduces Designer-RSI, a continual adaptation framework for agentic graphic design. Its core method involves a frozen frontier model interacting with design software and an external procedural memory that learns and refines reusable design skills from user traffic. The key contribution is the ability to evolve sophisticated design capabilities by accumulating and revising procedures based on execution outcomes, without requiring human labels or retraining the core model.
items.figure_caption: System overview. Left — rollout and reward. A brief (from a real User Prompt or in-context LLM Prompter) enters the graphic design agent; the Skill Bank retrieves the top skills with and filters the tool list. The agent executes a chain of tools through intermediate document states to an output image, which the grader turns into a scalar reward. Right — reflection and evolution. Per-skill statistics and recent call histories are the system’s assets; skills implicated in failures are edited or rewritten and bad histories are summarized into new skills, each verified by replay gate.

items.title: ChatGPT now knows what you do on other websites via ad collector
items.summary: ChatGPT can now track your browsing activity on other websites through an ad collector, potentially impacting user privacy.

items.title: Qwen Image 2.1

items.summary: Pirate Face is a new tool that helps users back up and restore large language models, preventing their accidental deletion.

items.title: US Revokes Limits on Power Plants' Climate Pollution
items.summary: The US has revoked regulations limiting climate pollution from power plants, a move that could significantly increase greenhouse gas emissions from the sector.

items.title: AI and the Destruction of the Creative Commons
items.summary: AI's reliance on vast datasets, often scraped without consent, threatens the spirit and sustainability of Creative Commons by undermining the value of original, licensed work.

items.title: The LLMentalist Effect (2023)
items.summary: The LLMentalist Effect describes how large language models, despite lacking true understanding, can convincingly mimic human-like reasoning and problem-solving, leading to a perception of intelligence.

items.description: The agent harness performance optimization system. Skills, instincts, memory, security, and research-first development for Claude Code, Codex, Opencode, Cursor and beyond.
items.summary: This repository provides an agent harness for performance optimization, featuring skills, instincts, memory, security, and research-first development for various AI coding assistants.

items.description: A framework for building agentic apps
items.summary: This framework enables developers to build agentic applications by providing tools and components for creating intelligent agents that can interact with their environment and perform tasks.

items.description: A coding-agent skill for multi-phase security audits with independently verified, machine-readable findings
items.summary: This Cloudflare skill enables multi-phase security audits by providing an agent that generates independently verified, machine-readable findings.

items.description: Scale computer-use 2.0 with open-source drivers, cross-OS fleets, and benchmarks for training, evaluation, and data generation.
items.summary: This repository provides an open-source framework for scaling computer usage with cross-OS fleets and benchmarks, enabling efficient training, evaluation, and data generation.
This repository provides a comprehensive framework and tools for building and deploying financial services applications, emphasizing security, scalability, and regulatory compliance.

items.description: A community-supported supercharged document management system: scan, index and archive all your documents
items.summary: Paperless-ngx is a community-driven document management system that allows users to scan, index, and archive all their documents efficiently.

items.description: Claude Code is an agentic coding tool that lives in your terminal, understands your codebase, and helps you code faster by executing routine tasks, explaining complex code, and handling git workflows - all through natural language commands.
items.summary: Claude Code is an AI-powered terminal agent that understands your codebase to accelerate development by executing tasks, explaining code, and managing Git via natural language commands.

items.description: Assignments for CS146S: The Modern Software Dev (Stanford University Fall 2026/2025)
items.summary: This repository contains assignments for Stanford's Modern Software Development course, focusing on practical projects and exercises to teach contemporary software engineering principles.

items.description: Fault-tolerant, highly scalable GPU orchestration, and a machine learning framework designed for training models with billions to trillions of parameters
items.summary: Higgsfield is a fault-tolerant, highly scalable GPU orchestration and machine learning framework for training massive models with billions to trillions of parameters.

A brief (from a real User Prompt or in-context LLM Prompter) enters the graphic design agent; the Skill Bank retrieves the top skills with and filters the tool list. The agent executes a chain of tools through intermediate document states to an output image, which the grader turns into a scalar reward. Right — reflection and evolution. Per-skill statistics and recent call histories are the system’s assets; skills implicated in failures are edited or rewritten and bad histories are summarized into new skills, each verified by replay gate.

papers.title: Accelerating Dense LLMs via L0-regularized Mixture-of-Experts
papers.abstract: This paper introduces L0-MoE, a method to accelerate dense LLMs by using L0-regularization to create a lightweight Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture. The core contribution is achieving significant speedups (up to 2.5x) with minimal performance degradation, outperforming existing acceleration techniques. This is enabled by domain-aware dataset curation and dynamic batching for efficient training.
papers.figure_caption: Overview of the L0-MoE Architecture, which includes three main stages: (1) cluster confusion matrix based sampling, (2) expert formation using L0 regularization, and (3) dynamic batching for MoE training. The figure above illustrates the process of building an L0-MoE with four experts over n n iterations of dataset sampling.

papers.title: CodeMidas: Scaling Agentic Coding RL Environments from Code Itself
papers.abstract: CodeMidas is a novel agentic pipeline that automatically generates reinforcement learning (RL) coding environments directly from existing source code. It leverages agents to explore functionality, create tests based on code execution, and validate tasks, enabling scalable creation of diverse coding challenges. This method significantly expands the range of extractable tasks compared to previous approaches, resulting in a large dataset of 5,545 training tasks across numerous languages and domains.

papers.title: Do Personality-Tuned LLMs Make Better Social Agents?
papers.abstract: This paper investigates if fine-tuning LLMs with personality data improves their social agent capabilities. By training on personality-labeled social media and dialogues, they created personality-based dialogue engines and evaluated their consistency and controllability against instruction prompting. The contribution lies in demonstrating that personality-aware fine-tuning can reduce the "alienness" of LLMs in social simulations by enhancing personality fidelity and providing interpretable behavioral outputs.

papers.title: ExpBoN: Exponential-Noise Best-of-$n$ for Efficient Test-Time LLM Alignment
papers.abstract: ExpBoN is a novel method for efficient Large Language Model (LLM) alignment at inference time. It uses an exponential-noise mechanism to achieve smoother control over the reward-distribution shift trade-off, leading to exponentially faster convergence in key metrics. This approach, integrated into guided speculative inference as ExpGSI, significantly reduces computational costs while maintaining alignment quality.
papers.figure_caption: Figure 3: Exact finite- n n convergence of ExpBoN vs. SBoN on real LLM candidate pools (medians with 10–90% bands). Columns: the reward score r / λ r/\( \lambda \) of Section 2 at the deployed temperature λ = 1 / 20 \( \lambda \)=1/20 and at λ = 1 / 2 \( \lambda \)=1/2 , the temperature of the synthetic example in Figure 1; the GSI score of Section 4 without clipping ( β ​ r + d \( \beta \) r+d ) and with clipping ( s C = β ​ r + min ⁡ ( d , C ) s_{C}=\( \beta \) r+\( \min \)(d,C) ; β = 20 \( \beta \)=20 , C = 0.45 C=0.45 ). Rows: KL divergence to the tilted target and relative centered-reward gap. Output laws are computed exactly by numerical integration; the dotted line marks numerical precision ( 10 − 13 10^{-13} ). ExpBoN converges geometrically in every configuration while SBoN decays polynomially; comparing the last two columns, clipping speeds up convergence by capping the right tail of the scores.

papers.title: An Interpretable Memory Decision Controller for LLM Agents Based on Three-Signal Complementarity: Decoupling Confidence and Consistency
papers.abstract: This paper introduces the Memory Decision Layer (MDL), a novel, parameter-free module for LLM agents. The MDL addresses the issue of conflicting memories in retrieval-augmented generation by employing a three-signal complementarity approach (relevance, reliability, task risk) to intelligently decide which memories to trust, thereby reducing hallucinations. Its core contribution is an interpretable decision representation that quantifies memory trustworthiness, decoupling confidence from consistency.
papers.figure_caption: Complete four-stage architecture of the Memory Decision Layer (MDL): 𝟏 \( \mathbf{1} \) multi-source input signals, 𝟐 \( \mathbf{2} \) orthogonal subspace encoding, 𝟑 \( \mathbf{3} \) the memory decision layer, and 𝟒 \( \mathbf{4} \) four-level action decision.

papers.title: CASCADE Against Jailbreaks: Combination Across Stages with Controlled Attack-Defense Evaluation
papers.abstract: This paper introduces CASCADE, a framework for systematically evaluating and combining defenses against LLM jailbreaks across different pipeline stages. It standardizes attack success rate measurement and query budgets to provide principled comparisons, revealing that layered defense combinations are more effective than single defenses and offer practical recommendations for robust LLM safety.

papers.title: A Lie Detector Test for Language Models: Reading Knowledge a Model Won't Reveal
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Probe of Internal Recognition (PIR), a method inspired by forensic concealed information tests to detect knowledge hidden within language models. PIR works by presenting a model with a question and multiple candidate answers, then analyzing its internal states to identify which answer it internally recognizes as correct, without needing external ground truth. This allows for the identification of a model's true knowledge, even when its output might be misleading.
papers.figure_caption: The PIR pipeline. We read each option’s last-token span, project onto the item-contrast direction, and take the highest-scoring option as the recognized answer. The divergence detector compares that answer against the model’s output.

papers.title: AutoViewMem: Self-Configuring Orthogonal Views for Conversational Long-Term Memory
papers.abstract: AutoViewMem addresses the challenge of organizing diverse information in LLM long-term memory by creating self-configuring, low-overlap semantic views. This data-driven framework disentangles information at write-time, improving the quality and relevance of memories for retrieval. Its core contribution is a representation-first approach that enhances consistency and personalization in conversational agents.
papers.figure_caption: The AutoViewMem architecture. The system processes a conversation stream through online view discovery, selects an orthogonal view set via DPP, and performs schema-guided memory extraction and retrieval to provide context for the LLM agent.

papers.title: Bayesian Belief Layer for Controllable Opinion Dynamics in LLM Agents
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Bayesian Chronicle Agents (BCA) to address the implicit opinion dynamics in LLM agents. BCAs separate an agent's beliefs from its speech, representing stances as probabilities updated via Bayesian inference. A single parameter, $κ$, controls stubbornness, enabling the generation of distinct opinion dynamics regimes like consensus or persistent disagreement.

papers.title: CIPL: A Channel-Aware Framework for Recoverable Privacy Leakage in LLM Agents
papers.abstract: This paper introduces CIPL, a novel framework for evaluating privacy leakage in LLM agents by considering the entire information flow from sensitive data to an attacker's observable output. Unlike previous methods, CIPL models the process through distinct stages and assesses recoverability under a shared protocol. Its contribution lies in providing a more realistic and nuanced understanding of privacy risks, demonstrating that leakage is not solely determined by data storage but also by the agent's operational pipeline and external observation capabilities.
papers.figure_caption: Leakage regimes under the shared black-box measurement protocol. Panel (a) reports CER, while panel (b) reports AER. Under CIPL, three recurring patterns emerge. Memory-based settings remain saturated across all five providers. rag_ctrl exhibits a frequent-but-partial leakage pattern, with high any-recovery but incomplete recovery across providers. Tool-mediated channels show stronger dependence on observation surface and provider behavior under LLM-in-the-loop evaluation: return_echo is generally stronger than args_exfil away from provider-level ceiling effects, while DeepSeek and GPT-4o approach or reach saturation on some tool channels. Values are means over five seeds.

papers.title: Detecting Pretraining Data in Large Language Models from a Free-Energy Perspective
papers.abstract: This paper proposes Energy Transfer Detection (ETD) to distinguish pretraining data in large language models. ETD improves upon existing methods by using an inclined boundary that considers both prediction loss and predictive entropy, effectively correcting for generalization. This approach offers a free-energy interpretation and demonstrates superior performance in detecting pretraining data.
papers.figure_caption: Motivation from the joint distribution of prediction loss and predictive entropy. Left: member texts (i.e., pretraining texts) and non-member texts (i.e., non-pretraining texts) may have overlapping token-level loss profiles. Right: during pretraining, a horizontal likelihood-only boundary may classify some predictable non-members as members, whereas an inclined boundary incorporating predictive entropy provides clearer separation.

papers.title: DiaVLo: Diagnosing Behaviours of Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: DiaVLo is a diagnostic framework that uses human input and VLMs' own generation abilities to create specifications of desired and observed model behaviors, highlighting any misalignments. It also provides causal estimates to pinpoint the key concepts driving these behaviors. This approach helps identify both aligned and misaligned behaviors, offering insights into how VLMs perceive, organize, and prioritize information.
papers.figure_caption: With DiaVLo , we frame VLM diagnosis as an addition to benchmarking, enabling the definition and verification of observed model behaviours with respect to specifications of desired behaviours.

papers.title: EnterpriseVal: Quantifying the Efficacy, Reliability and Value of Generative AI in the Enterprise
papers.abstract: This paper introduces EnterpriseVal, a system designed to bridge the gap between generative AI's capabilities and its actual business impact. It addresses the problem that current evaluations focus on model potential rather than enterprise-specific deployment readiness. EnterpriseVal provides a use-case-level evaluation framework that formalizes the socio-technical configuration and employs a comprehensive metric catalogue to assess fidelity, utility, efficiency, and reliability.
papers.figure_caption: Two gaps between public benchmarks and enterprise decisions. Capability benchmarks measure what a model can do on portable tasks. Enterprises must also establish transfer to their own workflows and ground truth (Gap 1) and convert quality metrics into a value-and-risk case a governance body can act on (Gap 2).

papers.title: NemotronLabs VoiceChat: An Open Full-duplex Speech-to-Speech Model with Tool Calling Capabilities
papers.abstract: NemotronLabs VoiceChat is an open, full-duplex speech-to-speech model that integrates tool-calling capabilities. Its core method involves a unified streaming architecture combining speech encoding, a decoder-only language model with parallel text and tool output streams, and a streaming TTS decoder. This design enables natural, real-time conversation with tool invocation and achieves state-of-the-art performance in handling interruptions and backchannels.

papers.title: Value-Sensitive Delegation in Everyday AI Agent Use: Evidence from OpenClaw
papers.abstract: This paper introduces "value-sensitive delegation," a new framework for understanding user interactions with AI agents. By analyzing Reddit posts about OpenClaw, the researchers found that users prioritize values related to the agent's operating conditions, not just its outputs. The study contributes by highlighting the importance of considering these user-defined conditions for successful and ethical AI agent deployment.

papers.title: From Pretraining to Proficiency: Real-World Subtask RL for Long-Horizon Manipulation with Minimal Human Intervention
papers.abstract: This paper introduces PARTS, a method to improve pretrained robot policies for complex, long-horizon manipulation tasks. It focuses RL training on specific failure-prone subtasks by using the pretrained policy for most actions and introducing learned selectors and verifiers to provide local rewards for successful subtask completion. This approach efficiently bridges performance gaps with minimal human intervention, even when full task success is rare.

papers.title: GraphSkillEvo: Evolutionary Optimization of Graph-Structured Agent Skills
papers.abstract: This paper introduces GraphSkillEvo, a novel method for optimizing LLM agent skills by representing them as structured graphs. This graph representation, with nodes for execution steps and edges for transitions, provides clearer workflow guidance and reduces redundancy compared to unstructured natural language skills. The core contribution is enabling more effective and efficient skill optimization by navigating a constrained, structured search space.
papers.figure_caption: Existing skill optimization methods (e.g., SkillOpt) maintain unstructured skills and optimize skills purely with LLM self-reflection, resulting in suboptimal performance. GraphSkillEvo solves this with graph-structured skills for giving more workflow-level guidance and providing a reduced search space for comprehensive population-based evolutionary search.

papers.title: SpecQuant: Speculative Decoding with Multi-Parent Quantization for Adaptive LLM Inference
papers.abstract: SpecQuant is a training-free framework that accelerates LLM inference on consumer hardware by combining speculative decoding with multi-parent quantization. It dynamically uses different quantized model variants (e.g., INT4, FP8, FP16) based on task complexity, reserving full-precision for demanding tasks. This adaptive approach allows for efficient inference without retraining or separate draft models, improving token acceptance for speculative decoding.

papers.title: Watermarkable Multi-Draft Speculative Sampling via Poisson Processes
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a novel multi-draft speculative sampling algorithm for LLMs, leveraging Poisson processes. Its core contribution is enabling both efficient inference and robust output watermarking simultaneously, overcoming a previously identified fundamental trade-off. The algorithm achieves this through an exact list-coupling scheme, leading to drafter invariance and improved sampling efficiency without compromising watermark embedding.
papers.figure_caption: The trade-off between watermark and efficiency on existing methods ( Hu and Huang, 2024 ) : Vanilla Speculative Sampling (VSpS), Maintain Watermark Strength (MWS), and Maintain Sampling Efficiency (MSE), and our algorithms (PFR, and multi-draft MPFR that is presented in Section 5 ). For both PFR (lower-left) and MPFR (upper), we embed watermark (measured by Average Negative Log P-value Per Token (ANLPPT)) without degrading the Average Accepted Tokens Per Step (AATPS). This figure uses Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct as the target and draft, respectively, on dataset cnn_dailymail . Experiments on more models and datasets are shown in Appendix D .

papers.title: Designer-RSI: Evolving Procedural Memory from User Traffic for Agentic Graphic Design
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Designer-RSI, a continual adaptation framework for agentic graphic design. Its core method involves a frozen frontier model interacting with design software and an external procedural memory that learns and refines reusable design skills from user traffic. The key contribution is the ability to evolve sophisticated design capabilities by accumulating and revising procedures based on execution outcomes, without requiring human labels or retraining the core model.
papers.figure_caption: System overview. Left — rollout and reward. A brief (from a real User Prompt or in-context LLM Prompter) enters the graphic design agent; the Skill Bank retrieves the top skills with and filters the tool list. The agent executes a chain of tools through intermediate document states to an output image, which the grader turns into a scalar reward. Right — reflection and evolution. Per-skill statistics and recent call histories are the system’s assets; skills implicated in failures are edited or rewritten and bad histories are summarized into new skills, each verified by replay gate.
